what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from South Korea in all host countries: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 630 South Korean asylum seekers, and Australia hosted 55.6% of them.
After Australia, the largest hosts are the United States, Brazil and Canada.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for South Korea, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2002 and 2019 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 2000 at 359 asylum seekers, and the figure fell to a low in 2011.
The figure was at its highest, 1089, at the end of 2024.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took.
These are year-end totals summed over every host country that reported to UNHCR.
